# QS-CFW-4376-34 Quality specification - valve body CFW-4376-34 (F316)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-4376-34

Scope

This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) machined from F316 forging stock at Plant P3. It defines critical quality requirements that must be met prior to release for assembly and shipment, and it establishes the accepted inspection methods, example acceptance criteria, and required records. Background information is provided to explain the rationale for each requirement and to aid inspection planning and nonconformance disposition.

Requirements table

| Requirement | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Hardness range | The hardness range for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 31-34 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is ±0.10 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 46.2 kg. |

Inspection method

Overview
- Inspectors must verify each item in the requirements table against the part and associated certification. The inspection sequence should ensure traceability from forging material to final inspected part. The inspection method described here explains equipment selection, calibration requirements rationale, measurement approach, and sample-record examples to be retained.

Hardness verification
- Rationale: Hardness is a proxy for microstructure and heat treatment effectiveness in F316 forgings. The specified hardness controls machinability and wear characteristics while ensuring the material has not been over-tempered.
- Method: Verify hardness using a Rockwell hardness tester calibrated to the appropriate scale for HRC readings. Test locations must be representative of critical wall sections and machined surfaces. Document test locations and results on the inspection record.
- Acceptance: The hardness must meet the hardness range for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 31-34 HRC. Any reading outside this range requires immediate hold of the affected lot and initiation of nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter verification
- Rationale: Bore form and tolerance affect sealing and assembly fit. The process capability of machining and finishing operations must produce bores within the stated tolerance to ensure functional performance.
- Method: Measure the bore using an appropriate bore gauge or plug gauge with calibration traceability. Report the measured diameter and directly compare to the nominal drawing dimension plus or minus the bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is ±0.10 mm. Record the measurement instrument ID and calibration reference on the inspection record.
- Examples: If a measured diameter deviates such that it exceeds the ±0.10 mm tolerance relative to the drawing nominal, flag the part as nonconforming and follow the nonconformance handling procedure in this document.

Forging weight verification
- Rationale: Maximum forging weight is controlled for material procurement, forging die capability, and handling equipment limits. Conformance prevents overloading of equipment and ensures process consistency.
- Method: Verify forging weight using the supplier certificate of conformance and cross-check with the receiving scale report. Confirm that the maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 46.2 kg is not exceeded for any unpackaged forging intended for this part number.
- Notes: If a forging exceeds the specified maximum, segregate the material and initiate nonconformance handling.

Calibration and equipment
- All measurement instruments used for verification must have up-to-date calibration certificates traceable to an accredited calibration laboratory. Record instrument ID, calibration date, and next-calibration status on the inspection form. Maintain a copy of the calibration certificate with inspection records.

Inspection records to keep
- Retain the following for each inspected lot: part identifier, heat/lot number, hardness readings with locations, bore measurements with instrument ID, forging weight verification notes and certificates, inspector name, and final disposition statement. Ensure records are stored in the document control system and linked to part CFW-4376-34 traceability files.

Nonconformance handling

Detection and immediate actions
- When a nonconformance is detected against any requirement in the requirements table, the inspector shall stop progression of the affected parts and mark the items clearly with a hold status. Provide a written hold tag referencing this document and the failed requirement.

Containment and segregation
- Segregate nonconforming parts from conforming inventory to prevent inadvertent use. Document the location and count of segregated items on the inspection record.

Evaluation and disposition
- Evaluate the nature and extent of the nonconformance through root-cause analysis. Consider rework options only if the corrective action will result in full compliance with the original specification without introducing other defects. Examples of acceptable dispositions include rework to an inspected and documented corrective process that restores compliance, acceptance under a documented engineering deviation, or scrap if recovery is not feasible.

Documentation and approval
- Document the nonconformance, evaluation, proposed disposition, and final approval in the quality system. Include supporting evidence such as hardness test plots, bore measurement logs, supplier certificates, and photographs where applicable. Approval for disposition must be recorded with signatory authority consistent with Plant P3 procedures.

Feedback and corrective action
- For systemic issues, initiate a corrective action to address root causes in forging, heat treatment, or machining processes. Track corrective actions until effectiveness is demonstrated and documented.

Retention of records
- Maintain nonconformance records with the inspection records tied to the affected part number CFW-4376-34 and reference this document identifier. Records must include the initial detection data and final disposition rationale.

Related documents
- None.
